stem: A small business requires an initial investment of Rs 33,000 and is expected to generate Rs 15,000 per year for the next 3 years. The discount rate is 12% per annum. [Given: PV annuity factor for 3 years at 12% = 2.4018] What is the NPV of this investment?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Adds undiscounted inflows 3 * 15,000 = 45,000 then subtracts outlay 33,000, getting 12,000 without applying any discounting.
Computes 36,027 - 33,000 = 3,027 correctly but reverses the subtraction order to 33,000 - 36,027, reporting -3,027.
Reports the undiscounted sum of inflows 3 * 15,000 = 45,000 without deducting the initial outlay.

explanation: NPV = PV of cash inflows - initial investment. A positive NPV means the project earns more than the required rate and should be accepted.

explanation_sections.punchline: NPV = (CF * PVAF) - C_0; the given annuity factor converts all future inflows to present value in one multiplication.
explanation_sections.approach: Name the formula NPV = CF * PVAF - C_0. Map: CF = Rs 15,000, PVAF = 2.4018, C_0 = Rs 33,000. Compute PV = 15,000 * 2.4018 = 36,027. NPV = 36,027 - 33,000 = 3,027 (positive, accept).
explanation_sections.lesson: Always discount future cash flows before comparing them to the initial outlay. Positive NPV = accept; negative = reject.
explanation_sections.timing: 20 seconds. The stem gives the factor; the only work is one multiplication and one subtraction. Watch for the sign.
